task.title: Measure startup, traversal, search and memory costs
task.problem: Existing aggregate timings do not identify dominant costs; proposed speedups are hypotheses. Reviewer-reported baseline (not reproduced here): 300 unique three-file trees, two runs/commit, 900 matches; mounting 15.5 s, search 0.095 s (one rg) versus 1.55 s (per-tree rg), wall 18.5 versus 20.0 s.
task.proposal: Create offline repeatable fixtures and a benchmark command separating fresh index, warm index, narrow glob, broad content and many identical source trees. Record versions, file/tree counts, peak RSS, mount count and process launches. Distinguish a fresh tool index from cold OS/BuildStream caches.
acceptance: Fixtures include many small files, few large files, many unique trees and duplicate trees.
Reports separate startup/load, traversal/index, mounts, rg search and output fan-out.
Benchmark writes only temporary caches and records repeat distributions rather than a single best time.
Establish baselines before adopting concurrency, SQLite or direct content blob search.
Reproduce the reported 300-tree fixture with exact runtime versions and compare serial versus small bounded pools before choosing concurrency.
Separate readiness-poll waiting from actual FUSE startup; ensure_mount currently polls every 50 ms, close to the reported 52 ms per tree.
evidence: scripts/bench_source_grep.py builds offline fixtures (20000 small files, 4x16 MiB files, 300 unique 3-file trees, 100 elements sharing one tree) in a temporary work directory and runs 9 scenarios with repeat distributions, per-phase timings, peak mounts, process counts and RSS.
Measured on Python 3.11.15, BuildStream 2.8.0, buildbox-fuse 1.4.15, ripgrep 14.1.0, 4 CPUs, Linux 6.18, as root; 3 repeats, medians.
Reviewer fixture reproduced on main 775a143: content-unique-trees wall 19.97 s, mount 15.43 s, search 1.61 s, deferred cleanup 1.54 s.
Direct buildbox-fuse probe (100 trees): mount ready 2.9 ms median, umount 2.0 ms, SIGTERM-driven unmount 0.85 ms. The fixed 50 ms readiness poll accounted for ~92% of the reported mount stage.
Bounded-pool prototype (mount+rg+unmount per tree, 300 trees): 1 worker 3.48 s, 2 workers 1.82 s, 4 workers 0.99 s, 8 workers 0.81 s; follow-up recorded as BSG-021.
tests/test_integration.py::test_benchmark_harness_smoke runs the tiny scale in CI.
